sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and file header
sections.what: The header explains that the script pulls the latest code, reloads modules and keeps running variables. Users see nothing when the file loads on its own.
sections.why: Likely reason: the header is there so the owner knows what the helper does before running it.
sections.watch_out: The header says to run this cell, but it is a plain Python file, and the last line runs the update as soon as it is loaded.

sections.name: auto_update_and_reload (part 1)
sections.title: Saving local changes and pulling code
sections.what: Finds the project folder, stashes uncommitted local changes, pulls one fixed branch from GitHub, and reports whether it was up to date, updated, or had issues.
sections.why: Likely reason: stashing lets the pull succeed when the working files have local edits.
sections.watch_out: The stashed local edits are never restored by this script, so they stay hidden until someone runs git stash pop.

sections.name: auto_update_and_reload (part 2)
sections.title: Reloading modules and checking variables
sections.what: Reloads the listed modules if they are loaded, re-imports the key classes, reports which notebook variables are still available, and prints a closing message.
sections.why: Likely reason: Python does not refresh already-loaded code by itself, so reloading is needed to use the new code.
sections.watch_out: Objects created before the update keep their old class code, so the notebook's setup cells must be run again to use the new version.

summary: A notebook helper that downloads the latest project code from GitHub and reloads Python modules so a running notebook uses the new code.
purpose: Lets the owner update the code without restarting the notebook.
why: The header states the purpose. Likely reason: restarting a long notebook session loses its variables, so this avoids that.
how: Finds the project root, stashes local changes, pulls one fixed branch from GitHub, reloads a fixed list of modules, re-imports key classes, reports which notebook variables still exist, and prints a final message. The last line runs the function as soon as the file is loaded.
inputs: The git project folder, network access to GitHub, the branch name written in the script, and the notebook's current variables.
outputs: Console messages; updated project files; reloaded modules in the running notebook.
risks: Stashed local changes are never restored by the script, so they can seem to vanish. The branch name is fixed in the code. Objects created before the update keep the old code.
debug: Run git stash list in a terminal to see hidden changes, then git stash pop to restore them. If the pull reports issues, read the message printed. If an import error appears, check that the module names match the project files. Restart the notebook kernel if old behavior persists.
